newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juncker says against talk of EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Juncker says against talk of EMU delay.

text.p: Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker said on Wednesday he was against the talk about the possibility of delaying European economic and monetary union.

"The treaty says that member states which meet the (Maastricht treaty) criteria will enter monetary union on January 1 1999," Juncker told a business lunch. "We must apply the treaty, nothing but the treaty and all of the treaty."
Referring to continuing speculation in some quarters that monetary union could be delayed, he said, "I am against this way of thinking currently being aired."
He also said that Europe must stop thinking of itself as two blocs, rich northern European states and southern European Union countries.
Germany in particular is seen as reluctant to admit southern EU countries to monetary union at the starting date.
"If they meet the criteria in March 1998, of course they will be admitted, just like France, like Luxembourg and the others," Juncker said.
Southern EU countries should not be treated as a group but as individual nations on their own merits, he said.
